subject: Reliability remedy offer and partial credit proposal
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara@finmore.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Cc: FinMore Procurement <procurement@finmore.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reliability incident: impact on renewal discussions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the quick post-mortem yesterday. I wanted to follow up in writing: the 37-minute outage during our peak batch window last week materially impacted our month-end reporting pipelines and triggered questions from our leadership about continuing with the current SLA.

We're approaching our renewal window in July and I need to present a clear remediation and commercial path that addresses two things for FinMore:
- A concrete reliability improvement plan (what will prevent recurrence in the next 90 days).
- A commercial remedy (credits / pricing / contractual commitments) that restores trust and justifies recommending renewal to our CFO.

Can Redwood propose a short-term credit structure and a roadmap for technical steps you will take? Procurement also wants an estimate for the incremental cost of moving to a higher-tier guarantee for the next 12 months.

I attached our outage timeline for reference (attachment: outage_log.csv).

Best,
Sara
Sara Li
VP, Platform Engineering
FinMore Inc

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Li <sara@finmore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability incident: impact on renewal discussions

Sara — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the timeline. I own this with my team and want to make sure you have a practical, time-bound proposal for the execs and procurement. High level:

1) Immediate commercial remedy (proposal):
   - A one-off service credit equal to 15% of the last 3 months' invoice, payable as an account credit to be applied to future invoices.
   - In addition, an operational credit: 10% discount on our Dedicated capacity SKU for the first 6 months if FinMore converts to Dedicated within 60 days.

2) Technical remediation plan (30/60/90):
   - 0-30 days: KV cache and burst routing tuning, add an emergency autoscale policy for the affected cluster; weekly stability reports to your SRE team.
   - 31-60 days: Deploy a hotfix to the request multiplexing layer and run a staged canary across 10% of FinMore traffic.
   - 61-90 days: Full rollout of improved routing + SLA re-verification with updated latency baselines.

3) Optional premium commitment: we can offer a bespoke SLO addendum (higher uptime target + financial SLA) if you choose Dedicated + 12-month commit. I will attach a draft addendum for review.

Ive included Marissa on commercial items and Neha on the SLO wording & verification plan. Attached: an internal credit breakdown (attachment: credit_breakdown.xlsx) and a quick addendum outline (attachment: addendum_draft.pdf).

Next steps: would you and procurement be available for a 30-minute call Monday to finalize numbers?

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: FinMore Procurement <procurement@finmore.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>, Sara Li <sara@finmore.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability incident: impact on renewal discussions

Rishi — we can do Monday. A couple of clarifying items for procurement:

- We need the exact formula you used to arrive at the 15% one-off credit. Procurement will want it quantified against invoice lines.
- For the Dedicated discount: what are the SKU names and the expected committed spend that unlocks the 10%?
- If we accept a 6-month discount, can the discount be extended if the stability targets are not met? (i.e., rolling credits tied to SLOs)

Please include the contract/legal contact and a draft of any amendment we should circulate internally.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
FinMore Inc

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Reliability incident: impact on renewal discussions

Heads-up — FinMore wants the math and the SKU list. Procurement also asked whether we can make the discount conditional/rolling based on SLOs. Suggested internal approach below before I call them at 11:00 PT:

- Commercial: we back the 15% credit with a straightforward calculation (sum of charges for M-1, M-2, M-3 * 15%). Offer to provide a worksheet.
- Dedicated SKUs: propose two tiers: "Dedicated-Standard" (reserved vCPU/GPU profile) and "Dedicated-Plus" (higher IO/latency SLA); 10% applies to Dedicated-Plus only, requires a 12-month reserve; otherwise 6% on Standard with 6-month commit.
- Rolling credits: we can structure 2% additional monthly credit applied retroactively if weekly stability targets are missed (up to cumulative 12%). This ties remediation to measurable SLOs.

Neha — can you draft a short SLO table (latency P50/P95 targets, uptime target, verification cadence) and a few lines for the addendum? Marissa — I'll need your approval on the credit numbers and the tier definitions.

If you want to adjust the numbers before I speak to procurement, reply-all quickly.

-Rishi

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Li <sara@finmore.com>, FinMore Procurement <procurement@finmore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Reliability remedy offer and partial credit proposal

Sara / Procurement — thanks for the call earlier. Per our discussion, here is the agreed summary so you can take it to finance and legal:

Agreed commercial remedies
- One-off account credit: 15% of FinMore's aggregate Redwood invoices for Mar/Apr/May 2026. Formula and worksheet attached (attachment: credit_breakdown.xlsx).
- Conditional Dedicated discount: 10% off Dedicated-Plus SKU for the first 6 months if FinMore signs a 12-month reserve within 60 days. If FinMore chooses Dedicated-Standard with a 6-month reserve, discount will be 6%.
- Rolling stability credits: If weekly SLO targets are missed, a 2% monthly credit will be applied retroactively for each missed week, capped at a cumulative 12% for the first 6 months.

Technical & verification commitments
- 30/60/90 remediation milestones as discussed; Redwood will provide weekly stability reports and a mid-point canary report (after 45 days).
- Neha will own SLO verification and provide an SLO table + acceptance criteria for legal.

Next steps
- Rishi to circulate an addendum draft (DocuSign link) for legal review within 48 hours.
- FinMore to confirm whether they prefer Dedicated-Plus or Standard by July 10 to lock pricing.

If this summary looks correct, we'll push a draft addendum to DocuSign and share the HubSpot deal update. Appreciate the constructive conversation — we want to make sure FinMore has a stable path forward while protecting both parties.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

(attachments: credit_breakdown.xlsx, addendum_draft.pdf)
